comment: The table of a build with --use: the reading of a used artifact in
src/fort/library/artifact.ft and std/linux/os.ft, the uses between the used
libraries and the link order in src/fort/library/graph.ft, the options, the link line and the
document files of src/fort/driver.ft, and the extern check of the modules
outside the closure in src/fort/modules.ft, src/fort/check.ft and
module-system.md 10.2 and 10.4). Each row breaks one rule. The module suites
compile the mutated module themselves; the build links the compiler so that
the md5 guard reads it, and the last stage runs test/library/use_test.py
over that compiler. The table runs in the VM with the default runner after
`tools/vm configure` and `tools/vm build`. The build waits 2 s and touches
the sources in the guest first, as tools/mutations/artifact_fort.json does.
D9.11-os-mode-shift-darwin survives in the VM, which builds the Linux root; a
native macOS host catches it with the run test of std.os (the ticket Log).
The D14.1-dash rows hold `-o -`: stdout under -S and -c, and a usage
error for a link and for an artifact (toolchain.md 1).
build: sleep 2 && touch src/fort/library/graph.ft src/fort/library/artifact.ft src/fort/driver.ft src/fort/modules.ft src/fort/check.ft src/fort/check_stmt.ft std/linux/os.ft && cmake --build build/Linux/debug --target fort

stages.name: the run test of std.os
stages.command: python3 test/lang/run_tests.py --fort build/Linux/debug/fort --std-dir build/Linux/debug/std --cc clang --target x86_64-linux-gnu run/stdlib/123_os_file_mode

stages.name: the module suites of --use
stages.command: python3 test/lang/run_tests.py --root test/fort --fort build/Linux/debug/fort --std-dir build/Linux/debug/std library/graph library/artifact_reading modules_outside driver_use driver_test driver_library

stages.name: the run corpus against std.flib
stages.command: python3 test/library/use_test.py --fort build/Linux/debug/fort --std-dir build/Linux/debug/std --cc clang --target x86_64-linux-gnu --opt opt-18
